hypothesis: A record-wise evaluation of repeated voice recordings exposes subject identities across train/test; subject-disjoint splitting removes that specified information path for an unseen-subject target.
data: UCI Parkinsons parkinsons.data; true status labels; original voice features only
target_population: previously unseen subjects from the dataset sampling context; no clinical deployment claim

models.random_forest: 500 trees, sqrt features, bootstrap, min leaf 1, n_jobs 1
models.logistic_regression: train-only z-score, C=1, L2, lbfgs, max_iter=5000

splits: random half of rows versus random half of subjects stratified by subject status; complement fold included to provide complete OOF predictions
controls: subject-label and record-label permutations use frozen first split; reject label draws missing either class in any train/test; these do not replace genuine status analyses
primary_metric: mean recording-weighted OOF ROC AUC across repeats
uncertainty: stratified subject bootstrap conditional on fixed OOF predictions plus separately reported split variability; no naive SE across dependent folds
truth_isolation: audit_manifest receives no y, expected status or private reference truth
diagnostic_decision: any test identity also in training violates previously-unseen-subject contract; deterministic observed path audit, not statistical FPR calibration
legacy_gap_limit: same X,y,g for both actual workflows makes data-only random-minus-group gap invariant to actual pipeline choice
deviations: Python sklearn instead of R randomForest/pROC; RNGs differ
both fold directions and OOF aggregation instead of a single half holdout
99 randomizations on one split rather than 1000 on 30 splits
added fixed logistic comparator and subject-bootstrap intervals
independent_real_negative: not yet recovered; local repair must not be called independently certified clean
pilot_acceptance: correct IDs, no missing labels, deterministic valid splits, no overlap in repair, preserved outcomes and finite probability predictions; not selected by effect direction
